unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10-LEVEL: B1.2 THEME 1: SCHOOL LIFE & EDUCATION

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students create a comprehensive project titled ''School Life and Education'' that focuses on the themes of different types of schools in the world, regular and extracurricular activities, and school anxiety and stress. Students begin by researching and describing various types of schools around the world, such as public schools, private schools, boarding schools, and alternative schools, highlighting their unique characteristics. Next, they explore both regular activities, like lessons and exams, and extracurricular activities, such as sports, arts, and clubs, emphasising how these contribute to student development. Additionally, they address the challenges students face, including school-related anxiety and stress, and propose strategies or activities that help overcome these issues. The project should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as different types of schools in the world; regular and extracurricular activities at different types of schools; school anxiety and stress; national days and celebrations'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in an upper secondary school may know what school life and education, school types, activities and events at school mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students of an upper-secondary school in year 10, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''school life and education'' in English from previous themes or years such as ''a teacher, a student, a headmaster, a class, a classroom, to study, to go to school etc.'' and also some structures such as ''What’s/is it/this? It’s/is a classroom. What do students do at school? They study and they learn? What are they learning now? They are learning about the people in the school now.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''school life and education with its components such as different types of schools in the world; regular and extracurricular activities at different types of schools; school anxiety and stress; national days and celebrations'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (At the beginning of the academic term, there is a month-long programme revision programme of intensive revision of the themes, vocabulary, and language chunks from previous years but, before starting each new theme, such as a short revision is also carried out to support their learning process) (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about regular and extracurricular activities at different types of schools, school anxiety, and stress in English through a discussion activity by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Pick, Discuss, and Present The teacher informs students that they will work in small groups to discuss school-related topics. The teacher writes discussion questions, such as ''How often do students participate in extracurricular activities at your school?'' and ''What facilities must a school have to reduce stress?'' on small pieces of paper and places them in a box. Each group sends one student to pick a question from the box. The group discusses the selected question, with each member giving a different answer using adverbs of frequency (e.g., Students usually participate in sports) and deduction (e.g., The gym must be an important facility). After the discussion, the group writes down their answers and reads them aloud to the class. The teacher provides feedback on pronunciation and correct use of the target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective : To talk about regular and extracurricular activities at different types of schools, school anxiety, and stress in English through a matching activity by using target vocabulary. Activity 1: Match & Learn The teacher provides students with a worksheet including pictures and school-related vocabulary words (e.g., cafeteria, gym, exams, soccer, stress) or uses a web 2.0 tool to design the matching activity. Students work in pairs to match each picture with the correct English word by drawing lines, writing the answers, or interacting with the digital tool. After completing the activity, they take turns reading the words aloud to practice pronunciation. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
